metadata.title: Why Did Higher Wages Buy Less?
metadata.description:
How can a daily wage rise while the basics become harder to afford? This illustrated Paper Detour follows a reconstructed London working-family basket from before the Black Death through the nineteenth century. It compares necessities with a labourer's daily pay, measured in modeled wage-days, and finds a reversal: prices could outpace wages. The figures describe selected historical estimates and a defined model, not every family's budget or a modern cost-of-living comparison.

Chapters will be added from the final edit so their times match the finished film.
